<notes>
kept -> base harness -> All three rollouts (base1, inv1, dom1) deployed the identical harness (745ba24861); both inv1 and dom1 candidates showed harness.diff as "(no change)". Both candidate proposers independently concluded KEEP_BASE after evaluating their own rollouts. Base1 delivered a complete, systematic geometric analysis (28160 tokens, answer D); inv1 and dom1 delivered complete analyses with different output (23924, 22074 tokens, answer L). The difference is not in harness behavior but in LLM variance across independent samples—same harness produces different outputs depending on model sampling, not due to control flow or prompt structure. The candidates' proposers did not identify a failure mode, inefficiency, or breakdown in the current harness that would justify adding procedural guidance or other changes. The library (ood-geometric_shapes-168) shows procedural guidance reduced tokens 51% in a *different* task (baseline 58k); this task's baseline is already at 28k—more efficient than the library's improved endpoint (28.9k). No moment in the trajectories shows the harness failing to support the agent's reasoning; both trajectories show systematic, verifiable geometric analysis. Adding procedural text to address model variance would be speculative (no causal connection shown) and would burden context on every run for a problem the proposers did not identify.
</notes>

KEEP_BASE
